Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

HelpSteer2: Open-source dataset for training top-performing reward models (2406.08673v1) · paper method: Each HelpSteer2 response initially receives three annotator ratings; if their helpfulness range exceeds two points, two more annotators are recruited. The source reports a mean of 3.41 annotators per sample and approximately 1,000 US-based annotators engaged through Scale AI.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

HelpSteer2: Open-source dataset for training top-performing reward models (2406.08673v1) · paper method: The workflow retains the three most-agreeing ratings from up to five, adds QA and removes responses whose helpfulness spread remains above two points. Approximately half of all collected annotations were excluded overall, leaving 21,362 responses to 10,681 prompts; helpfulness quadratic-weighted Cohen κ rises from 0.465 initially to 0.791 after postprocessing.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

HelpSteer2: Open-source dataset for training top-performing reward models (2406.08673v1) · paper method: With two-epoch regression reward-model training on HelpSteer2, global batch size 128, validation-loss checkpoint selection and model-specific learning-rate search, the paper reports RewardBench overall accuracy 88.8% for Llama 3 70B and 92.0% for Nemotron-4 340B; overall is the mean of four categories over 2,985 tasks and excludes optional Prior Sets.

cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.rewardbench

  • This selected-version benchmark result is not reproduced here and is not a claim of current leaderboard rank.
  • Reported training uses AdamW and MSE loss with ten warmup steps; selected constant learning rates are 2e-6 for 70B and 7e-7 for 340B, searched over {1,2,3,4,5}e-6 and {1,3,5,7,9}e-7 respectively.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

HelpSteer2: Open-source dataset for training top-performing reward models (2406.08673v1) · paper method: The limitations identify English-only and exclusively US-based annotation, possible cultural bias, uneven attribute combinations, compute-dependent tuning and uncertain transfer of conclusions from large language models to smaller models.
